name: Farm Pond Fish Stocking Calculator
seoTitle: Farm Pond Fish Stocking Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: A farm pond is usually stocked in a ratio, not a single species: bluegill as forage, bass as predators, and often channel catfish alongside. Free farm pond fi
summary:
A farm pond is usually stocked in a ratio, not a single species: bluegill as forage, bass as predators, and often channel catfish alongside. It returns total fish to stock, predators, forage fish and fish per hectare, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator turns pond surface area into a stocking plan — total fish, the predator-to-forage split and the biomass it implies. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Farm Pond Fish Stocking
sections.html:
Total fish = pond area (ha) × stocking rate (fish/ha); predators = total × predator share

The symbols in the formula

sections.title: How do I use the Farm Pond Fish Stocking?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: predator share of 20%, presence of wild fish (1 = yes, 0 = no) of 0.

Substituting them into the formula gives total fish to stock of 1,000 fish, predators of 200 fish, forage fish of 800 fish, fish per hectare of 2,500 fish/ha, pond surface area of 0.4 hectares, stocking rate of 2,500 fish/ha.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
1,000 – 2,500 /haLightunfertilised pond, natural productivity only
2,500 – 5,000 /haStandardfertilised pond with a bass-bluegill balance
above 5,000 /haIntensiveneeds aeration and feeding

  • The classic bass-bluegill plan stocks forage first and predators a season later, so the forage population is established before anything eats it.

  • If wild fish are already present, stock larger fingerlings and expect lower survival.

  • Pond depth matters as much as area: 1.5–2 m over most of the pond, with deeper water for overwintering, is the usual minimum.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Stocking predators and forage at the same time in a pond with no cover.
  • Applying a hatchery's per-acre rate to a hectare (or the reverse) — a factor of 2.47.
  • Stocking before the pond has cycled and the food chain has established.

faq.q: How many fish per acre should I stock?
faq.a: A common starting point is 1,000 fish per acre (about 2,500 per hectare) in a fertilised pond, split roughly 80% forage to 20% predators.
Yes at low densities with good depth and vegetation control; above about 5,000 fish/ha, summer oxygen becomes the limiting factor.

faq.q: What does the Farm Pond Fish Stocking actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns total fish to stock, predators, forage fish and fish per hectare. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
